resources.string: How a Game Boy Advance, PlayStation or Nintendo 64 game fills the screen. Keep shape: as large as it goes in its own shape, with borders. Whole pixels: a whole multiple of its picture, every pixel the same size; sharper, with wider borders. Stretch: the whole screen, out of shape. A game can have its own (its Options). Applies the next time a game starts. (RECOMP_SCALE)

How the picture of a Game Boy Advance, PlayStation or Nintendo 64 game is enlarged. Sharp: square pixels, as on the console\'s screen. Smooth: softened edges. Console default: sharp for the Game Boy Advance, smooth for the PlayStation and the Nintendo 64. A game can have its own (its Options). Applies the next time a game starts. (RECOMP_FILTER)

How finely a PlayStation or Nintendo 64 game draws its picture. Native: the console\'s own resolution. 2x, 4x, 8x: that many times more pixels each way, for sharper edges (textures stay the console\'s); each step asks much more of the device, try 2x first. 8x: the Nintendo 64 Vulkan renderer only; a PlayStation game stops at 4x. A game can have its own (its Options). Applies the next time a game starts. (RECOMP_UPSCALE)

Hold the rewind hotkey (Select + L2 by default, R on a keyboard) to go back in time in a Game Boy Advance, PlayStation or Nintendo 64 game, without sound; let go and the game goes on from there. On (not N64): on for the Game Boy Advance and the PlayStation, off for the Nintendo 64, where keeping the history asks more of the device. A game can have its own (an N64 game can turn it on). Applies the next time a game starts. (RECOMP_REWIND)

How much memory the rewind history may use: more goes further back. With 64 MB a Game Boy Advance game usually goes back a minute or more, a PlayStation game some tens of seconds; the oldest moments go first. A game can have its own. Applies the next time a game starts. (RECOMP_REWIND_MB)

A look for a game\'s picture (Xbox, Game Boy Advance, PlayStation, Nintendo 64), drawn at the screen\'s resolution. None: the picture as it is. Sharp bilinear: square pixels without uneven widths when the scale is not whole. Scanlines: the dark lines of a TV. CRT: scanlines and the red, green and blue stripes of a TV tube. LCD grid: the pixel grid of a handheld\'s screen (none on an Xbox game). A game can have its own (its Options). Applies the next time a game starts. (RECOMP_SHADER)

How marked the picture shader\'s lines or grid are. Shader default: scanlines and LCD grid 50 %, CRT 60 %. No effect with None or Sharp bilinear. Applies the next time a game starts. (RECOMP_SHADER_STRENGTH)
The CRT shader\'s screen bulges like a TV tube, with darker corners. Only with the CRT shader. Applies the next time a game starts. (RECOMP_SHADER_CURVATURE)

The LCD grid shader keeps a trace of the previous picture, as a handheld\'s slow screen did (some games count on it for transparency). Only with the LCD grid shader. Applies the next time a game starts. (RECOMP_SHADER_GHOSTING)

On: the controller vibrates when the game asks for it (the PlayStation DualShock, the Nintendo 64 Rumble Pak, the Xbox pad). Off: never. For every console. Applies the next time a game starts. (RECOMP_RUMBLE)

How this game fills the screen: as in Settings › Graphics › Scale, or its own. Keep shape: as large as it goes in its own shape. Whole pixels: every pixel the same size, wider borders. Stretch: the whole screen, out of shape. Applies the next time the game starts. (RECOMP_SCALE)

Frame generation for this game: as in Settings › Graphics › Frame generation, or on or off for it alone (the multiplier and the shader set stay Settings\'). Frames the game shows twice or three times are replaced by drawn in-between ones, so a game at 30 frames per second shows 60; a game that already shows 60 is left as it is. Pictures appear about one game frame later. Applies the next time the game starts. (RECOMP_LSFG)

How finely this game draws its picture: as in Settings › Graphics › Internal resolution, or its own. Native: the console\'s resolution. 2x, 4x, 8x: sharper edges, much more work for the device. 8x: the Nintendo 64 Vulkan renderer only; a PlayStation game stops at 4x. Applies the next time the game starts. (RECOMP_UPSCALE)
How this game\'s picture is enlarged: as in Settings › Graphics › Picture filter, or its own. Sharp: square pixels. Smooth: softened edges. Applies the next time the game starts. (RECOMP_FILTER)
Saved for this game; it applies the next time the game starts
%1$s\n\nFor this game alone: as in Settings, or a value of its own. Applies the next time the game starts.
The buttons this game plays with: the mapping of all games, or one of its own (Mapping for › This game only, in its Controls). A opens its Controls.
Every value of %1$s follows Settings again: its own values, its own controls and its theme go. Its saves stay.
